raw_graphql_pull_request.body: First of all, this is WIP, so any suggestion is welcomed. ### Summary * Adds one CUDA kernel that computes the DSA indexer scores of every visible key and selects each row's top-2048 keys **without materializing the `[rows, keys]` logits matrix**. * One call covers a prefill chunk of up to 16,384 query rows and up to 1M keys. The dense path needs up to 127 call pairs (`fp8_mqa_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`) for the same chunk. * Opt-in (`VLLM_USE_FUSED_MQA_TOPK=1`, default 0). The dense path is unchanged and remains the default and the fallback. ### Motivation: what materializing the scores costs The dense prefill path writes the fp32 scores of every (query row, visible key) pair to HBM, then reads them back to select the top-k. One 16,384-row prefill chunk needs `16,384 × keys × 4 B` of logits: | Keys | Logits for one 16K-row chunk | Dense calls under the 512 MiB budget | Logits HBM traffic (write + read) | |---|---|---|---| | 16K | 1 GiB | 2 | 2 GiB | | 128K | 8 GiB | 16 | 16 GiB | | 512K | 32 GiB | 64 | 64 GiB | | 1M | 64 GiB | 127 | 128 GiB | This produces the following pattern: Which can become increasingly concerning the larger the context, e.g. ISL 512K: Two consequences: 1. **The logits budget trades KV-cache capacity against indexer speed.** During memory profiling, `sparse_attn_indexer` allocates a dummy `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` buffer, so the logits budget is part of the peak memory the KV cache is sized from. On GLM-5.x with an FP8 KV cache, one token costs 47.7 KB per GPU (78 MLA layers × 576 B + 21 indexer layers × 132 B; MLA KV is replicated across TP ranks). Measured at startup (TP4, B300, `--max-model-len 1048576`): | Configuration | Available KV memory | KV cache tokens | |---|---|---| | Dense, 512 MiB budget (default) | 115.66 GiB | 2,603,456 | | Dense, 8 GiB budget | 109.23 GiB | 2,458,816 (−5.6%) | | Fused (this PR) | 115.37 GiB | 2,596,928 (−0.25%) | At the default budget the logits buffer fits under the profiling run's other peak allocations, so it costs no KV cache. The cost is speed: rows per dense call shrink as keys grow (2²⁷ / keys), so a 128K-token prefill in 16K-token steps needs 76 dense call pairs and a 1M-token prefill needs 4,217, against 8 and 64 fused calls. Buying fewer dense calls means raising the budget, and that memory comes straight out of the KV cache. An 8 GiB budget (one dense call per 16K-row chunk at 128K keys) costs 144,640 tokens of KV cache. One dense call per chunk at 1M keys would need 64 GiB, more than the KV cache of the entire 1M-token sequence (46.6 GiB). The fused kernel gets single-call chunks at every length for a fixed 296 MiB workspace. 2. **The logits round trip is pure overhead.** Only 2048 of the `keys` scores per row are needed. The fused kernel keeps only a gated candidate set: in shared memory up to 16K keys, and above that about 3K–7K candidates per row at 6 B each, i.e. about 0.3–0.7 GB written per 16K-row chunk, versus 16–128 GiB of logits traffic at 128K–1M keys. ### What this PR does ### Memory * Fused workspace: a pool of 2 eight-row slots per SM, fixed size, independent of rows, keys and context. It is 296 MiB on a 148-SM B300, allocated once per device during the profiling run, so it is accounted against the KV cache: −6,528 tokens (−0.25%) versus dense at the default budget (table above). * With the fused path enabled and `max_model_len ≤ 1M`, no prefill chunk can reach the dense path, so the profiling run skips the dense logits dummy buffer. On GLM-5.x this changes nothing measurable, because that buffer sits under the profiling peak, but it no longer reserves memory the fused path never uses. ### Performance (Work in Progress) **Kernel.** B300, real GLM-5.x indexer inputs captured from serving (MRCR 2- and 8-needle and random prompts, layers 0, 9 and 19), one 16,384-row prefill chunk, median of `do_bench_cudagraph(rep=200)` over captures. Dense is chunked by the 512 MiB budget exactly as in vLLM and captured in one CUDA graph. Integrated vs dense (DeepGEMM logits + `top_k_per_row_prefill` on current main): | Keys | Rows | Captures | Dense (ms) | Fused (ms) | Speedup, median (range) | Fused exact topK | Dense exact topK | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4K | 4096 | 3 | 0.092 | 0.069 | 1.31× (1.31–1.44) | 3/3 | 0/3 | | 8K | 8192 | 6 | 0.293 | 0.297 | 0.99× (0.91–1.12) | 6/6 | 0/6 | | 16K | 16384 | 12 | 0.979 | 0.930 | 1.06× (0.88–1.17) | 12/12 | 0/12 | | 32K | 16384 | 9 | 2.62 | 2.43 | 1.05× (1.00–1.21) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 64K | 16384 | 9 | 6.12 | 4.71 | 1.29× (1.22–1.36) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 128K | 16384 | 9 | 13.0 | 8.76 | 1.49× (1.41–1.53) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 256K | 16384 | 9 | 27.8 | 16.9 | 1.63× (1.58–1.66) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 448K | 16384 | 9 | 62.8 | 29.0 | 2.20× (2.11–2.22) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 512K | 16384 | 6 | 78.4 | 32.8 | 2.40× (2.34–2.42) | 6/6 | 0/6 | | 944K | 16384 | 3 | 246 | 58.9 | 4.18× (4.13–4.21) | 3/3 | 0/3 | | 1M | 16384 | 3 | 280 | 62.0 | 4.52× (4.38–4.55) | 3/3 | 0/3 | **End to end.** GLM-5.2/5.3-NVFP4, TP4, B300, FP8 KV cache, ### Accuracy MRCR shows no accuracy difference. Fused and dense agree within noise in every context range. Context | Samples | Fused | Dense | Difference -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 0–8K | 103 | 0.394 | 0.335 | +0.059 (+0.9σ) 8K–16K | 98 | 0.220 | 0.148 | +0.072 (+1.5σ) 16K–32K | 101 | 0.416 | 0.380 | +0.036 (+0.5σ) 32K–64K | 98 | 0.495 | 0.484 | +0.011 (+0.2σ) 64K–128K | 99 | 0.789 | 0.713 | +0.076 (+1.4σ) 128K–256K | 101 | 0.768 | 0.791 | −0.022 (−0.5σ) 256K–512K | 100 | 0.724 | 0.779 | −0.054 (−1.1σ) 512K–1M | 97 | 0.683 | 0.683 | 0.000 All | 797 | 0.561 ± 0.016 | 0.539 ± 0.016 | +0.022 (+1.0σ) ### Related Work This kernel's sampled gate is inspired by LiteTopK (#48726, arXiv:2607.11976): indexer scores concentrate in a narrow range, so a sampled threshold can discard most keys before the top-k. I open a separate PR because: * **Scope:** LiteTopK fuses only single-request chunks of exactly 8192/8128 rows with 192K–1M keys. Other chunks keep dense chunking, and even a fused chunk needs a separate seed-logits launch and about 2.6 GiB of workspace. Here every eligible chunk (≤ 16384 rows, ≤ 1M keys, multi-request) is one launch with no logits buffer and a 296 MiB workspace. * **Correctness:** on B300 (commit `c7184685`) I found an undersized shared-memory allocation (4100 memcheck errors), racecheck hazards in the candidate ring and the seed/radix-select kernels, and no recovery from candidate-buffer overflow (the mapping kernel traps). LiteTopK's selection is also approximate (99.998% recall); this PR matches dense up to boundary ties. * **Gain on B300:** the only B300 serving data in #48726 shows TTFT within ~1% of stock at ~200K tokens. This PR measures 1.10× at 256K and 2.05× at 1.04M (different setups, so not like-for-like). The PR credits LiteTopK (arXiv:2607.11976) as the inspiration for the sampled gate where it is implemented. However, the scoring half of this kernel is largely an adaptation of DeepSeek's code. This PR replaces the logits write-out with a sampled gate, candidate emission and in-kernel top-k selection.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Single-launch fused MQA-logits + top-k prefill vs the dense indexer path."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.attention.dsa.fused_mqa_topk import (
+    fused_mqa_topk_available,
+    fused_mqa_topk_prefill,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder
+
+requires_fused = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or not fused_mqa_topk_available(),
+    reason="Requires the SM100 fused MQA+top-k extension",
+)
+
+TOPKS = (512, 1024, 2048)
+TOPK = 2048
+LOGITS_BUDGET = 512 * 1024**2
+
+
+def _dense(q, k, scales, weights, starts, ends, topk=TOPK):
+    """Upstream dense path: budgeted DeepGEMM logits + top_k_per_row_prefill."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer import as_fp32_logits
+    from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
+        fp8_fp4_mqa_logits,
+        mqa_logits_mx_inputs,
+        mqa_logits_use_mx_scales,
+    )
+
+    k_scale = scales
+    if mqa_logits_use_mx_scales():
+        # Power-of-two scales as four equal UE8M0 bytes, like the K cache.
+        exp = torch.log2(scales).round().to(torch.int64) + 127
+        k_scale = (exp * 0x01010101).to(torch.int32)
+    rows = q.shape[0]
+    out = torch.full((rows, topk), -1, device=q.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    lens = ends - starts
+    max_len = max(1, int(lens.max()))
+    step = max(1, LOGITS_BUDGET // (4 * max_len))
+    for i in range(0, rows, step):
+        j = min(rows, i + step)
+        q_scale, w = mqa_logits_mx_inputs(q[i:j], None, weights[i:j])
+        logits = as_fp32_logits(
+            fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(
+                (q[i:j], q_scale), (k, k_scale), w, starts[i:j], ends[i:j], max_len
+            ),
+            lens[i:j],
+        )
+        # Compressed logits: row r holds keys [starts[r], ends[r]) from column 0.
+        ops.top_k_per_row_prefill(
+            logits,
+            torch.zeros_like(lens[i:j]),
+            lens[i:j],
+            out[i:j],
+            j - i,
+            logits.stride(0),
+            logits.stride(1),
+            topk,
+        )
+    return out
+
+
+def _logits(q, k, scales, weights, starts, ends):
+    """fp32 reference scores: sum_h w * relu(q . k) * scale, -inf off-range."""
+    kf = k.float()
+    out = torch.zeros(q.shape[0], k.shape[0], device=q.device)
+    for h in range(q.shape[1]):
+        out += weights[:, h, None] * torch.relu(q[:, h].float() @ kf.T)
+    out *= scales[None]
+    n = torch.arange(k.shape[0], device=q.device)
+    off = (n[None] < starts[:, None]) | (n[None] >= ends[:, None])
+    return out.masked_fill(off, -torch.inf)
+
+
+def _check(rel, q, k, scales, weights, starts, ends, scores=True):
+    """Indices relative to the row start: count, bounds, uniqueness, scores.
+
+    ``scores`` compares the selected scores with the exact fp32 top-k; the
+    SM100 dense path rounds its logits to bf16, so it is checked without.
+    """
+    topk = rel.shape[1]
+    visible = (ends - starts).clamp(min=0)
+    valid = rel >= 0
+    assert (valid.sum(1) == visible.clamp(max=topk)).all(), "valid count"
+    assert (rel[~valid] == -1).all(), "padding must be -1"
+    idx = rel.long() + starts[:, None].long()
+    assert ((~valid) | ((idx >= starts[:, None]) & (idx < ends[:, None]))).all()
+    srt = idx.masked_fill(~valid, -1).sort().values
+    assert ((srt[:, 1:] < 0) | (srt.diff(dim=1) > 0)).all(), "duplicates"
+    if not scores:
+        return
+    # Check scores in row blocks so the reference logits stay small.
+    step = max(1, LOGITS_BUDGET // (4 * k.shape[0]))
+    for i in range(0, q.shape[0], step):
+        j = min(q.shape[0], i + step)
+        logits = _logits(q[i:j], k, scales, weights[i:j], starts[i:j], ends[i:j])
+        ref = logits.topk(topk, dim=1).values
+        chosen = logits.gather(1, idx[i:j].clamp(min=0)).masked_fill(
+            ~valid[i:j], -torch.inf
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            chosen.sort(descending=True).values, ref, rtol=2e-4, atol=1e-4
+        )
+
+
+def _inputs(rows, keys, seed=913):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    q = torch.randn(rows, 32, 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    k = torch.randn(keys, 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scales = torch.ones(keys, device="cuda")
+    weights = torch.randn(rows, 32, device="cuda") / 32
+    return q, k, scales, weights
+
+
+@requires_fused
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", TOPKS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "keys,rows,case",
+    [
+        (4096, 64, "causal"),

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Single-launch fused FP8 MQA-logits + top-k prefill selection (SM100 family).
+
+One kernel (``torch.ops._C.fused_mqa_topk_prefill``) scores every visible key
+of each query row with the DeepSeek sparse-attention indexer and selects the
+row's top-k keys (k = 512, 1024 or 2048), without materializing the
+``[rows, keys]`` logits matrix that the dense path (``fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`` +
+``top_k_per_row_prefill``) needs.
+
+Above 4K keys the kernel is persistent (one CTA per SM); each CTA owns two
+8-row candidate slots. The scratch (~296 MiB on a 148-SM GPU) is allocated once
+per device and reused by every call, independently of the number of rows or
+keys.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEADS = 32
+FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEAD_DIM = 128
+FUSED_MQA_TOPK_TOPKS = (512, 1024, 2048)
+# Largest query chunk / gathered key range a single call accepts.
+FUSED_MQA_TOPK_MAX_ROWS = 16384
+FUSED_MQA_TOPK_MAX_KEYS = 1 << 20
+
+_CANDIDATES_PER_ROW = 16384
+_RETAINED_PER_ROW = 4096
+_SLOTS_PER_SM = 2
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FusedMQATopKWorkspace:
+    """Caller-owned scratch of the fused kernel (see fused_mqa_topk.cu)."""
+
+    counter: torch.Tensor  # [2] int32, zero between calls (the kernel restores it)
+    values: torch.Tensor  # [8S, 16384] fp16, S = 2 slots per SM
+    indices: torch.Tensor  # [8S, 16384] int32
+    retained: torch.Tensor  # [8S, 4096] fp32
+    retained_indices: torch.Tensor  # [8S, 4096] int32
+    counts: torch.Tensor  # [16384] int32, per-row candidate counts
+    defer: torch.Tensor  # [16384 / 8] int32, blocks queued for the exact rescan
+
+    def as_args(self) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        return (
+            self.counter,
+            self.values,
+            self.indices,
+            self.retained,
+            self.retained_indices,
+            self.counts,
+            self.defer,
+        )
+
+
+_WORKSPACES: dict[int, FusedMQATopKWorkspace] = {}
+
+
+def fused_mqa_topk_available() -> bool:
+    """True when the fused op is compiled in and the GPU is SM100-family."""
+    return (
+        current_platform.is_cuda()
+        and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+        and hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_mqa_topk_prefill")
+    )
+
+
+def get_fused_mqa_topk_workspace(device: torch.device) -> FusedMQATopKWorkspace:
+    """Return the per-device workspace, allocating it on first use.
+
+    The block counter is zeroed once; every launch leaves it zeroed again.
+    """
+    index = (
+        device.index
+        if device.index is not None
+        else torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    )
+    ws = _WORKSPACES.get(index)
+    if ws is None:
+        dev = torch.device("cuda", index)
+        num_sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(index).multi_processor_count
+        slots = _SLOTS_PER_SM * num_sms
+        rows = FUSED_MQA_TOPK_MAX_ROWS
+        ws = FusedMQATopKWorkspace(
+            counter=torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
+            values=torch.empty(
+                (8 * slots, _CANDIDATES_PER_ROW), dtype=torch.float16, device=dev
+            ),
+            indices=torch.empty(
+                (8 * slots, _CANDIDATES_PER_ROW), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev
+            ),
+            retained=torch.empty(
+                (8 * slots, _RETAINED_PER_ROW), dtype=torch.float32, device=dev
+            ),
+            retained_indices=torch.empty(
+                (8 * slots, _RETAINED_PER_ROW), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev
+            ),
+            counts=torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
+            defer=torch.empty(rows // 8, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
+        )
+        nbytes = sum(t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in ws.as_args())
+        logger.info(
+            "Allocated fused MQA+top-k workspace on cuda:%d (%d slots, %.1f MiB).",
+            index,
+            slots,
+            nbytes / 2**20,
+        )
+        _WORKSPACES[index] = ws
+    return ws
+
+
+def fused_mqa_topk_config_supported(q: torch.Tensor, topk_tokens: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether this indexer's query layout and top-k fit the fused kernel."""
+    return (
+        topk_tokens in FUSED_MQA_TOPK_TOPKS
+        and q.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        and q.dim() == 3
+        and tuple(q.shape[1:]) == (FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEADS, FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEAD_DIM)
+        and q.is_cuda
+        and fused_mqa_topk_available()
+    )
+
+
+def fused_mqa_topk_supported(
+    q: torch.Tensor, k: torch.Tensor, topk_tokens: int
+) -> bool:
+    """Static eligibility of an indexer prefill chunk for the fused kernel."""
+    return (
+        k.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        and k.dim() == 2
+        and k.shape[1] == FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEAD_DIM
+        and 0 < q.shape[0] <= FUSED_MQA_TOPK_MAX_ROWS
+        and 0 < k.shape[0] <= FUSED_MQA_TOPK_MAX_KEYS
+        and fused_mqa_topk_config_supported(q, topk_tokens)
+    )
+
+
+def fused_mqa_topk_key_scales(scales: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Per-key fp32 scales from the indexer K cache.
+
+    SM100 caches store each power-of-two scale as four equal UE8M0 bytes in an
+    int32; the fp32 value 2**(e - 127) has bit pattern ``e << 23``.
+    """
+    if scales.dtype == torch.int32:
+        return ((scales & 0xFF) << 23).view(torch.float32)
+    return scales
+
+
+def fused_mqa_topk_prefill(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    starts: torch.Tensor,
+    ends: torch.Tensor,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    rows_start_at_zero: bool = False,
+) -> bool:
+    """Fused replacement of ``fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`` + ``top_k_per_row_prefill``.
+
+    q: [rows, 32, 128] fp8 e4m3; k: [keys, 128] fp8 e4m3; scales: [keys] fp32;
+    weights: [rows, 32] fp32; starts/ends: [rows] int32, the visible key range
+    ``[start, end)`` of each row; output: [rows, k] int32 with k (the top-k)
+    512, 1024 or 2048.
+
+    Writes the same convention as ``ops.top_k_per_row_prefill``: indices
+    relative to the row's ``start`` (i.e. ``key - start``), unordered, ``-1``
+    padded when fewer than k keys are visible. ``rows_start_at_zero=True``
+    promises every ``start`` is 0 (single-request chunk) and skips the
+    relative-index conversion.
+
+    Returns False (and leaves ``output`` untouched) for unsupported inputs so
+    the caller can fall back to the dense path.
+    """
+    rows, keys = q.shape[0], k.shape[0]
+    if (
+        not fused_mqa_topk_supported(q, k, output.shape[1] if output.dim() == 2 else 0)
+        or scales.dtype != torch.float32
+        or scales.numel() != keys
+        or weights.dtype != torch.float32
+        or tuple(weights.shape) != (rows, FUSED_MQA_TOPK_HEADS)
+        or starts.dtype != torch.int32
+        or ends.dtype != torch.int32
+        or starts.numel() != rows
+        or ends.numel() != rows
+        or output.dtype != torch.int32
+        or output.shape[0] != rows
+    ):
+        return False
+
+    logger.info_once(
+        "Using the single-launch fused MQA+top-k prefill kernel "
+        "(FP8, 32 heads, top-k %d).",
+        output.shape[1],
+    )
+    q = q.contiguous()
+    k = k.contiguous()
+    scales = scales.contiguous()
+    weights = weights.contiguous()
+    starts = starts.contiguous()
+    ends = ends.contiguous()
+
+    # The kernel writes the output with 16-byte stores; any other layout goes
+    # through a temporary (never the case for the indexer's own buffers).
+    direct = output.is_contiguous() and output.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+    out = (
+        output
+        if direct
+        else torch.empty_like(output, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+    )
+    ws = get_fused_mqa_topk_workspace(q.device)
+    # The kernel emits absolute key indices; the dense top-k (and the sparse
+    # attention consumer) use indices relative to the row start. relative=True
+    # converts in place (rows with start 0 are skipped on the GPU).
+    torch.ops._C.fused_mqa_topk_prefill(
+        q,
+        k,
+        scales,
+        weights,
+        starts,
+        ends,
+        out,
+        *ws.as_args(),
+        not rows_start_at_zero,
+    )
+    if not direct:
+        output.copy_(out)
+    return True
